rules: See XAX_SPEC.md section 21. Levels are derived from evidence by compiler/src/xax_replacement.py (validator v3, ADR-207); missing fields are UNIMPLEMENTED; every non-UNIMPLEMENTED label cites repository evidence; documents, sources, scripts, and images alone never support EXECUTED/MEASURED/PROVEN; MEASURED performance needs raw samples; an R4 runtime verdict (the row's `competitive` entry) is recomputed from raw samples: the XAX median must be at most 0.9999x the fastest non-XAX median and significantly faster. R5 is autonomous maintenance and R6 a proven 100% XAX-developed application; ai_tokens is historical/future-milestone evidence and gates no level.

platforms.name: x86-64 Windows
platforms.summary: Direct PE32+ executables executed on Windows 11; Win64 calls and callbacks, linear thread-handle lifecycle, and kernel32 loader imports.
platforms.runtime_requirement: none; kernel32 imports only where the program declares foreign calls
blockers: kernel32 packages cover 12 calls including a Win64 callback and linear thread-handle lifecycle; no files, sockets, or PE exports
float/aggregate functions still use the legacy allocator or frame path (ADR-095)
record links / pointer_rebase executed under Wine only (ADR-098), not on a Windows host
C baseline only under Wine with a start-up-bound fixture (ADR-100); no Windows-host or run-time-bound comparison
no PDB/unwind data; SIMD absent

platforms.name: Android (arm64-v8a)
platforms.summary: Direct DEX, manifest, resources, signed APKs, JNI shared objects, and libxposed API-102 modules executed under Vector v2.2. On Pixel 8 Pro the stateful counter app's cold start ties its Java + NDK, Java, and Kotlin twins (all within 2.5%, ADR-253), and the AArch64 jsonmin image runs at 0.956x NDK clang -O2 -static (ADR-254); the cold-start tie keeps the row at R3.
platforms.runtime_requirement: ART + platform-required DEX entry adapters, generated by the compiler; libxposed modules additionally need a libxposed API-102 framework, with Vector v2.2+ as the tested reference (ADR-178, executed on hardware in ADR-197)
blockers: R4 (ADR-253): cold start ties. All four arms installed side by side, six fresh installs each, 15 interleaved rounds per install (90 cold starts per arm): XAX 202.5 ms, Java + NDK 205.0, Java 200.0, Kotlin 202.0 median TotalTime, so XAX is 1.0125x the fastest arm and no arm is significantly faster than another; start-up is framework-bound. The AArch64 jsonmin image leads NDK clang and rustc on the same phone (0.956x, ADR-254), but R4 needs every cited workload to lead

libxposed API-102 modules execute under Vector v2.2 on Pixel 8 Pro hardware (ADR-197): 18 of 27 harness checks PASS, 0 FAIL, including discovery, native_init, hook result/argument replacement, retained handles, and API-102 hot reload with stable IDs; nine checks that need a breakpoint or a call (package callbacks, intercept, deopt order, manual unhook, module services, remote preferences/files, protective) are UNEXECUTED because attaching JDWP aborts Vector-hosted ART on API 37

native file/thread/socket contracts execute on Pixel 8 Pro arm64 hardware (ADR-173); any managed class whose methods forward to XAX JNI exports (lifecycle, callback interfaces, value-returning callbacks) executes there (ADR-199), but XAX code calling SDK members over JNI, exact JNI float values, NDK media/audio imports, and manifest permissions are not yet executed (their contracts and build rules are structural since ADR-202 to ADR-204)
one DEX per class costs 1.17x the twin's DEX bytes (an edit-locality choice)

platforms.name: AArch64 bare metal
platforms.summary: AAPCS64 images with a QEMU `virt` board package (reset/fault stubs, vector table, one interrupt source); executed under QEMU only.
platforms.runtime_requirement: none; the board image contains only the generated reset stub, fault stub, and vector table (ADR-128)
blockers: executed only under QEMU (semihosting harness and the virt board), not hardware (OI-44)
one board package (QEMU virt) and one interrupt source; no DMA program or nested interrupts; no static storage shared by handler and reset entry
static linking covers an AArch64 relocation subset (no GOT, TLS, or PLT forms) and freestanding objects only

not_applicable.dynamic_linking: a bare-metal board image has no loader; foreign code is linked statically into the image (ADR-129)

platforms.name: WebAssembly (wasm32)
platforms.summary: Direct module emission with no imports; executed in a host WebAssembly engine.
blockers: emitted modules have no imports: no WASI, no browser/DOM bindings, no generated JS glue
indirect calls absent; recursive functions cannot use stack allocations or aggregates (no shadow stack yet; scalar recursion executes, ADR-125)

platforms.name: WebAssembly + WASI
platforms.summary: wasm32 modules with three WASI imports (args, `fd_write`, exit); executed under Node.js `node:wasi`.
platforms.runtime_requirement: platform-required WASI host (Node.js node:wasi in current evidence)
blockers: three WASI imports only (args_sizes_get, fd_write, proc_exit); no files/clocks/sockets
provenance-carrying pointers in memory (OI-37) absent
recursive functions cannot use stack allocations or aggregates (no shadow stack yet; scalar recursion executes, ADR-125)

platforms.name: SIMT accelerator packet
platforms.summary: Synthetic deployment-packet format checked by conformance tests only; no execution.
blockers: synthetic packet target only; no SPIR-V/PTX/Metal/DXIL emission or physical GPU execution

platforms.name: x86-64 Linux
platforms.summary: Direct ELF64 executables via syscalls, optionally with declared shared-library imports; jsonmin executes as the R3 application. R4 (ADR-212 run): filestat 0.852x and jsonmin 0.959x clang -O2, chains 0.911x rustc -O3, all significant on one shared host; jsonmin's margin is small (an earlier binary measured 0.968x and 1.029x in two runs). R5: one jsonmin maintenance cycle through semantic transactions (ADR-213). R6: xb64, an application developed and maintained only in XAX (ADR-210).
platforms.runtime_requirement: none for the static profile; the dynexec profile requests ld.so explicitly and loads only declared DT_NEEDED libraries
blockers: R4 scope (ADR-212 run, one shared 4-vCPU Xeon host, 31 interleaved runs per arm): filestat 0.851851x clang -O2 (p=3.4e-7), jsonmin 0.959479x clang -O2 (p=0.031), chains (xax-soa) 0.911278x rustc -O3 (p=0.0094). jsonmin's lead is small: its previous binary measured 0.967682x and 1.029472x in two runs (§15.30, §15.32), so a re-run on another host may withhold R4 again. jsonmin's stripped binary is 1.21x clang's (17,616 vs 14,552 bytes). Float/aggregate functions still fall back to the older paths (OI-38)
no threads, signals, sockets, clocks packages; no DWARF
jsonmin writes its output with one write call (no partial-write loop)

R5/R6 scope: one jsonmin maintenance cycle (one constant edit, ADR-213) and one small XAX-only application (xb64, ADR-210), both by the session's agent; not yet repeated by an independent agent or on a larger application

platforms.name: AArch64 Linux
platforms.summary: Static and dynamic ELF executables. The static jsonmin image runs on two phones' Android kernels: on Pixel 8 Pro (Tensor G3) 0.956x NDK clang -O2 -static, the fastest non-XAX arm, and on the original Pixel (Snapdragon 821) 0.898x, ahead of rustc -O3 on both, over 101 interleaved pinned rounds each (ADR-254). Dynamic images and the filestat application run only under qemu-aarch64 (Android has no glibc loader).
platforms.runtime_requirement: none for the static profile; the dynexec profile requests /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 explicitly and loads only declared DT_NEEDED libraries
blockers: R4 scope (ADR-254): one workload (jsonmin, static profile) on two devices, a Pixel 8 Pro and an original Pixel (android_jsonmin_pixel1_evidence.json: Snapdragon 821, kernel 4.4, 0.898444x), whose Android kernels run the Linux AArch64 image; baselines are the NDK's clang -O2 (bionic, dynamic and static) and rustc -O3 for aarch64-linux-android, since a glibc toolchain's dynamic images cannot load there; a cross-check pinned to a Cortex-A715 core gives 0.924x (android_jsonmin_cpu80_evidence.json). Dynamic images and filestat (zlib through glibc's loader) are executed only under qemu-aarch64 user mode (OI-44)

code size: the jsonmin image is 18,044 bytes, 2.4x the dynamically linked clang binary (7,480 bytes stripped, plus bionic's libc.so) and 0.043x the static one; small leaf callees are inlined into the lowering view (ADR-254)
the register path covers integer and pointer functions, recursion groups, and borrowed-view returns (ADR-254); floats and aggregates still take the frame path
no TLS, unwind/DWARF, argv/env, threads, atomics, or C-callable XAX entries on this profile; R5: no maintenance record on this row

platforms.name: macOS / iOS / iPadOS / watchOS / tvOS / visionOS
platforms.summary: Not started: no Mach-O container, Apple ABI package, or Objective-C runtime contract.
blockers: no Mach-O container, Apple ABI package, or Objective-C runtime contract

platforms.name: RISC-V (RV64IM)
platforms.summary: Raw position-independent images, LP64 integer calls; executed under the Unicorn emulator; the XAX-hosted RISC-V backend and store verifier reach component fixed points here (S-steps, not B milestones).
platforms.runtime_requirement: none: raw position-independent RV64IM image, LP64 integer convention, no loader, relocation, or data section (ADR-113)
blockers: executed only under the Unicorn RV64 emulator, not hardware; no Linux/RTOS executable container or syscall package
integer subset only: no floats (F/D), raw memory outside lent views, atomics, vector (V), or indirect calls; aggregates of scalar fields only as made values and call results (views profile, ADR-151)
collatz kernel 3.72x clang -O2 emulated instructions and 3.23x code bytes (no compare/branch fusion or copy coalescing yet)

platforms.name: JVM
platforms.summary: Direct class files in a deterministic JAR with typed JDK member calls; linear memory, aggregates, sums, stack allocations, indirect calls, links, atomics, callbacks, object/array construction, and fields; native-plus-JNI strategy and JDK metadata imports. R4 for one workload: jsonmin's median is 0.865x the fastest non-XAX arm (javac), significant over 15 interleaved fresh-JVM runs per arm (re-run after ADR-212). R5 for one maintenance cycle (ADR-209): an AI agent raised jsonmin's depth limit through one semantic transaction, then the JAR was rebuilt, tested, benchmarked, and the store committed. The former AI-token trials are historical (ADR-207).
platforms.runtime_requirement: platform-required JVM (HotSpot 21 in current evidence); the JAR's Main-Class is a compiler-generated main(String[]) that calls the proof-only XAX entry (ADR-112; on the memory profile on a thread with a 256 MiB stack, ADR-156); linear memory and stream I/O are generated static members of the program's own class; no XAX runtime classes
blockers: R4 scope: one application (jsonmin) on one shared x86-64 host, OpenJDK 21 defaults, whole-process time of a fresh JVM; baselines javac and kotlinc (XAX_BENCHMARKS.md section 15.0a, ADR-157/158); one workload does not establish universal leadership

code size: jsonmin's program class is 1.49x javac's and 0.99x kotlinc's (5,575 vs 3,730 and 5,649 bytes, ADR-158); its JAR is 2.2x javac's one-class JAR, 0.001x the kotlinc JAR with the Kotlin runtime; the rest of the javac gap is the program's shape (inlined parser, packed results, a checked view per access), not the lowering

linear memory (ADR-156) is one byte[] with int offsets: freed blocks are never reused, at most 2^31 - 1 bytes; the general profile (ADR-159) has a fixed 1 MiB shadow stack; atomics are sequential because one XAX thread runs (ADR-160), so a profile with JVM-to-XAX callbacks from other threads needs real JVM atomics

R5 scope (ADR-209): one maintenance cycle of one application (jsonmin's depth limit, a one-constant edit inside a recursion group) by the session's AI agent; the harness replays the agent's edit against the pinned root, so the record is reproducible but the agent's choice is not re-made. No multi-edit, structural, or interface change has been maintained this way yet. The former AI-token trials (ADR-176 to ADR-201; best fair result 0.995x, multi-file 1.68x) are historical evidence for the deferred AI-efficiency milestone
R6: no complete deployable application developed and maintained 100% in XAX

platforms.name: .NET CLI/CLR
platforms.summary: Not started: no CLI metadata/IL container.
blockers: no CLI metadata/IL container

platforms.name: Browser (WebAssembly + generated glue)
platforms.summary: wasm32 page whose JavaScript glue is compiler-generated from imported `xax-web-v1` declarations; four DOM bindings executed.
platforms.runtime_requirement: platform-required browser JavaScript host; the page script is compiler-generated from the imported xax-web-v1 declarations only (ADR-103)
blockers: four bindings (query, body text read/write, body click); no element addressing, timers, fetch, canvas, or WebGPU
no Web IDL importer (OI-32); no static storage, so cross-event state lives in the DOM
no comparison against Emscripten/Rust wasm toolchains (R4)
recursive functions cannot use stack allocations or aggregates (no shadow stack yet; scalar recursion executes, ADR-125)

platforms.name: GPU (SPIR-V/Vulkan; PTX, Metal, DXIL planned)
platforms.summary: Direct SPIR-V compute modules executed on Mesa llvmpipe (a CPU Vulkan driver), not GPU hardware; integer words only.
platforms.runtime_requirement: the platform's Vulkan loader and driver (platform-required) create the pipeline and launch it; the module carries only the compiler-generated entry adapter, status binding, and trap stores (ADR-124); the host side is a test harness, not an XAX program
blockers: executed only on Mesa llvmpipe (a CPU Vulkan implementation), not hardware (OI-34, OI-44)
SPIR-V/Vulkan only; no PTX, Metal, or DXIL package
dispatch-loop lowering: Collatz is 6.9x an equivalent glslang kernel on llvmpipe; structured lowering of reducible CFGs is next
integer words only: no floats, 64-bit integers, calls, workgroup memory, barriers, or atomics
no XAX host program: Vulkan instance, buffers, and dispatch come from a test harness (R2)

not_applicable.dynamic_linking: a SPIR-V module is loaded whole by the Vulkan driver; there is no symbol-level dynamic linking

platforms.name: RTOS / embedded MCU (Cortex-M, RISC-V MCU)
platforms.summary: Not started: no MCU target, vector table, or linker-layout package.
blockers: no Cortex-M/RISC-V MCU target, vector table, or linker-layout package
